summary: NASA’s twin ESCAPADE probes have successfully completed dual Earth flybys and are now officially en route to Mars. In military space developments, France awarded an Airbus and Thales joint team a contract valued at over €1.5 billion ($1.7 billion) for new military Earth-observation satellites, while the U.S. Space Force selected Viasat for a $450 million contract to construct a unified network operations center. In civil space infrastructure, NASA chose Viasat, SES, and Astranis to provide Ka-band space relay capabilities compatible with its Tracking and Data Relay Satellite system. In commercial launch developments, Rocket Lab increased pricing for its Neutron launch vehicle ahead of a planned 2027 debut. Scientific highlights include a NASA study demonstrating how gravitational waves can be used to detect undiscovered exoplanets, as well as new research leveraging the James Webb Space Telescope to explain mysterious early-universe "little red dots." Looking ahead, launch tracking observers should monitor SpaceX as technicians conduct pad testing on the Starship Flight 15 Super Heavy booster ahead of an upcoming double-catch landing attempt.
